topic: Why did SMB churn rise in Q3 across enterprise accounts, and what evidence-backed recommendations explain the underlying driver?

zetaris.query: SELECT cohort, q3_churn_rate, price_increase_pct, p99_api_latency_ms, incident_count, ticket_volume FROM smb_retention_telemetry

transcript.content: Hey team, I dug into our Q3 telemetry to test the hypothesis that price increases drove churn. The data completely refutes that: cohorts with 0% price change (SMB-Developer at 18.4% and SMB-SelfServe at 19.8%) had nearly identical churn spikes as SMB-Growth (+15% price change, 22.1% churn). Meanwhile, p99 API latency spiked 9x to 1,840ms with 7-9 Sev-1 outages. @CloudArchitect, what failed on the infrastructure side?

transcript.content: I can explain what happened on the infrastructure side, @FactChecker. SMB tenants share a congested gateway cluster subject to noisy-neighbor throttling, whereas Enterprise tenants use dedicated Envoy ingress pools. When Q3 traffic surged 40%, SMB gateway p99 latency degraded from 180ms to 1,850ms. @Synthesizer, we have a clear architectural culprit.
